title: Damped oscillator: energy decay and sampling checks
turns: Create an original schematic of a horizontal spring-mass-damper system, with displacement, velocity and force arrows clearly labelled as schematic. Give a Markdown table of explicitly synthetic SI parameters and initial conditions for an underdamped example.

Derive the homogeneous damped oscillator solution in LaTeX and its mechanical energy derivative. Distinguish underdamped, critically damped and overdamped regimes; state parameter units and sign assumptions.

Write complete runnable standard-library Python for the analytic displacement and velocity in all three regimes, including the critical limit. Include executable tests for initial conditions, zero damping and invalid mass or negative damping.

Compare the analytic solution with step-refined numerical integration in a Markdown error table. Audit whether the discrete energy is monotone and explain how numerical error can imitate physical energy injection. Use only synthetic data.

Write a Chinese-English reproducibility report containing equations, full code and negative tests. Explain aliasing when recording oscillations and why the schematic image cannot verify force balance or identify physical damping parameters.

title: Control-flow graphs: dominators and independent certificates
turns: Define a synthetic directed control-flow graph with a named entry, a branch, a join, a loop and an unreachable node. Provide Markdown tables of nodes and edges. Define precisely which nodes participate in dominance.

Express the dominator fixed-point equations in LaTeX over entry-reachable nodes. Explain initialization and prove termination and correctness, distinguishing a fixed point from a path-based dominance claim.
Write complete runnable standard-library Python to validate the graph and compute dominator sets by fixed-point iteration. Include executable tests and deterministic ordering.
Trace each iteration for the synthetic graph in a Markdown table. Derive immediate dominators and explain the strict-dominator ordering that makes them unique for reachable non-entry nodes.

Implement an independent certificate checker using reachability after vertex removal instead of the fixed-point recurrence. Reject missing nodes, invented nodes, incorrect entry dominance and false dominance claims.

Enumerate all tiny directed graphs up to a clearly bounded size and compare the fixed-point solver with the independent checker. Provide full deterministic Python, finite bounds and an honest complexity estimate.

Add executable tests for self-loops, duplicate edges, an entry with incoming edges, disconnected cycles, unknown endpoints and a one-node graph. State the policy for unreachable nodes and show how the checker enforces it.

Write a Chinese-English audit including definitions, proof, complete solver/checker code and negative tests. Explain why dominance alone does not prove variable liveness, correct SSA construction or semantic equivalence of compiler optimizations.

title: Polarization optics: Jones vectors and power conservation
turns: Create an original schematic of a synthetic optical bench with an ideal linear polarizer, a quarter-wave plate and an analyzer. Label propagation direction and optical axes; distinguish schematic arrows from measured light fields. Give a Markdown table of synthetic angles and normalized input powers.

Derive the Jones matrices and transmitted intensity in LaTeX for a stated phase convention. Explain global phase, normalized polarization vectors and when Jones calculus cannot represent partially polarized light.

Write complete runnable standard-library Python using complex numbers to compose the matrices and compute intensity. Include executable tests for unitary retarders, crossed polarizers, Malus law and invalid normalization.

Provide a Markdown table sweeping analyzer angles for linear and circular input. Independently check power bounds and angle periodicity, including degree-versus-radian negative tests. Use explicitly synthetic values only.

Write a Chinese-English audit with formulas, full reproducible code and negative tests. Distinguish lossless retarders from lossy polarizers and explain why a schematic image cannot certify actual polarization, alignment or optical power.

title: Bipartite matching: augmenting paths and vertex-cover certificates
turns: Define a small synthetic bipartite assignment graph with named left and right vertices, at least one isolated vertex and competing choices. Give Markdown tables for vertices and edges. Distinguish maximum-cardinality matching from a maximal matching.
Define augmenting paths in LaTeX and prove why their absence characterizes maximum matching. State the bipartite partition assumptions and explain the symmetric-difference argument.
Write complete runnable standard-library Python that validates a bipartite graph and computes a maximum matching via augmenting paths. Include deterministic traversal and executable tests.

Trace each augmentation on the example in a Markdown table showing the matching before and after, the alternating path and its cardinality. Include an example where a greedy maximal matching is suboptimal.
Derive a minimum vertex cover using alternating reachability from unmatched left vertices. Prove that it covers every edge and has the same size as the maximum matching.

Implement an independent certificate checker for matching validity, edge coverage and equal cardinality. Reject repeated endpoints, nonedges, invented vertices and uncovered edges, including executable negative tests.

Enumerate every graph for a bounded tiny bipartition and compare the solver against brute-force matching and vertex-cover enumeration. Provide complete deterministic Python and explicit computational bounds.

Write a Chinese-English audit containing the proof, full solver and independent checker, tables and negative tests. Explain why this unweighted graph exercise does not solve weighted assignment, capacity constraints or real-world allocation fairness.

title: RC step response: transient energy and numerical convergence
turns: Create an original educational illustration of a series resistor-capacitor circuit connected to a switched DC voltage source. Label current direction and capacitor voltage; state that the illustration is schematic, not measured data.

For an initially uncharged 100 microfarad capacitor charged through a 2.2 kilohm resistor by a 5 V ideal source at t=0, derive the differential equation and analytic current and capacitor voltage. Define the time constant and show equations in LaTeX.

Calculate capacitor voltage, current, stored energy, and cumulative resistor dissipation at t/tau=0, 0.5, 1, 2, and 5. Present a Markdown table with units and verify source energy equals capacitor energy plus resistor heat.

Write self-contained standard-library Python using explicit Euler integration at dt/tau=0.1, 0.05, and 0.025. Compare against the analytic solution, print maximum voltage error, and check the approximate energy-balance residual. Include the code in a fenced block.

Discuss numerical stability, first-order convergence, and why an ideal charging circuit dissipates half the final source energy in the resistor even for a small positive resistance. Finish with a bilingual English/Chinese summary and a table separating ideal assumptions from real parasitics.

title: Convex hull: exact orientation and independent containment witnesses
turns: Use the planar integer points [(0,0),(4,0),(4,4),(0,4),(2,2),(1,0),(4,2),(2,4),(0,2),(0,0),(3,1)]. Define the signed orientation determinant in LaTeX and explain how its sign classifies a turn.

Derive Andrew’s monotone-chain convex hull algorithm. State a deterministic convention: remove duplicate points, return extreme vertices counterclockwise beginning at the lexicographically smallest vertex, and omit intermediate collinear boundary points.
Work through the sorted points and record lower-hull stack pushes and pops in a Markdown table. Explain the determinant and removal condition at each nontrivial pop.

Provide self-contained standard-library Python implementing the hull with exact integer arithmetic. Include executable assertions for the expected hull, all-identical points, two points, and a fully collinear set in fenced code.

Construct an independent certificate checker that verifies every original point lies in or on the returned convex polygon using exact orientation tests. Explain special handling of hulls with fewer than three vertices and include Python.
Prove the O(n log n) time bound, including why each point is popped at most once per chain. Distinguish sorting cost, stack traversal, and certificate-checking complexity in a Markdown table.

Show an explicit example where a naive fixed epsilon for floating-point orientation can change a hull decision. Explain translation, scaling, exact arithmetic, and robust predicates without claiming one universal epsilon works.
Conclude with a bilingual English/Chinese audit of vertex order, duplicates, collinear boundaries, containment, and numerical assumptions. Include the final hull and a compact invariant table.

title: Acoustics: Doppler shifts and sign conventions
turns: Create an original educational illustration of a moving sound source approaching a stationary observer in still air. Label wavefront spacing, velocity directions and the medium reference frame; mark the drawing schematic.

Derive the classical acoustic Doppler equation with explicit sign conventions for source and observer velocities. Use LaTeX and distinguish sound propagation through a medium from relativistic light shifts.
For sound speed 343 m/s and source frequency 440 Hz, compare approaching and receding source speeds of 10, 20 and 30 m/s. Give a Markdown table with units and explain the stationary limit.
Write self-contained standard-library Python to compute these shifts with validated subsonic inputs, including tests for stationary source and observer. Put code in a fenced block.
Explain how wind, acceleration and finite observer distance affect the assumptions. Finish with an English/Chinese summary and a table separating measured quantities from idealizations.

title: Chinese remainders: compatible noncoprime systems
turns: Solve x congruent to 2 modulo 6 and x congruent to 5 modulo 9. State the compatibility condition for noncoprime moduli and describe the full solution class.
Derive the two-congruence merge algorithm using Bezout coefficients. Use LaTeX to prove both necessity and sufficiency of the gcd compatibility condition.
Give a Markdown table comparing systems (2 mod 6, 5 mod 9), (2 mod 6, 4 mod 9) and (0 mod 4, 2 mod 6), including gcd, compatibility and resulting modulus.
Implement extended Euclid and generalized CRT in self-contained Python. Normalize negative residues, reject nonpositive moduli and return an explicit incompatibility result.
Extend the algorithm to merge a list of congruences and prove its invariant. Explain why the result modulus is the lcm rather than always the product.
Construct deterministic tests for modulus one, repeated moduli, negative residues, incompatible residues and an empty system. List expected results in a table.
Write a brute-force checker for small moduli and cross-check every pair of moduli from 1 through 8 against the merge implementation. Explain the finite verification bound.
Provide a bilingual English/Chinese worked example with three compatible congruences, a merge trace table, and a final substitution certificate for each original congruence.

title: Enzyme kinetics: initial-rate saturation and assumptions
turns: Generate an original educational illustration of a fictional enzyme binding a substrate and releasing a product. Label the catalytic cycle and distinguish schematic icons from molecular structures or measured data.
Derive the Michaelis-Menten initial-rate equation with the quasi-steady-state approximation. Define all constants in LaTeX and state the assumptions on substrate depletion and product inhibition.
For Vmax=120 micromolar/min and Km=30 micromolar, tabulate initial rates at substrate concentrations 0, 10, 30, 90 and 300 micromolar. Include fractional saturation in a Markdown table.

Write standard-library Python to compute rates and the sensitivity to Km and Vmax, validating nonnegative substrate and positive Km. Include exact half-saturation and zero-substrate tests in fenced code.

Explain why a saturation curve alone does not establish a molecular mechanism and compare competitive versus uncompetitive inhibition. Finish with a bilingual English/Chinese summary and an assumptions table.

title: Edit distance: dynamic programming and alignment certificates
turns: Compute the unit-cost Levenshtein distance between kitten and sitting. Define insertion, deletion and substitution and give one optimal edit sequence.
Derive the dynamic-programming recurrence and base conditions in LaTeX. Explain what each table cell certifies about prefixes.

Implement self-contained Python returning both distance and an edit script. Define deterministic tie-breaking and explain how edits refer to changing string positions.
Prove optimal substructure and termination. Analyze time and memory bounds, including the difference between retaining a full alignment and computing distance alone.

Give tests for empty strings, identical strings, repeated symbols, Chinese text and an emoji containing multiple code points. State whether the implementation measures code points or grapheme clusters.

Write a standard-library brute-force checker for binary strings of length at most three and compare it against the dynamic program. Include a function applying each returned script to verify the target.
Summarize in English and Chinese with a worked alignment table, a certificate that the script cost equals the computed optimum, and limitations for transpositions and Unicode normalization.

title: Porous media: Darcy flux, head gradients and travel time
turns: Create an original educational cross-section of a fictional saturated sand column between two water reservoirs. Label head levels, column length, cross-sectional area and flow direction. Mark it schematic rather than measured geological data.
Derive Darcy discharge from hydraulic conductivity and the head gradient, using LaTeX with explicit units and sign conventions. Distinguish discharge, Darcy flux and pore-water velocity.

For conductivity 2e-5 m/s, column length 1.5 m, area 0.02 m^2 and porosity 0.35, compare head drops 0.05, 0.15 and 0.30 m. Provide a Markdown table of flow rate, pore velocity and nominal travel time.
Write self-contained standard-library Python to calculate these values. Validate physical inputs, include the zero-gradient case and explain the infinite travel-time limit with fenced code.

Explain why preferential flow, dispersion, unsaturated conditions and changing porosity limit the simple model. End with a bilingual English/Chinese summary and a table separating assumptions from observations.

turns: Trace disjoint-set unions (0,1), (2,3), (1,2), (4,5), (3,5) over elements 0 through 6. Give the resulting partition and explain the difference between a representative identifier and a semantic component label.
Define parent-forest, root and size invariants in LaTeX. Explain why union by size preserves acyclicity and how path compression changes the forest without changing the partition.
Provide a Markdown trace table of parents and root sizes after every union, breaking equal-size ties by the smaller root identifier.
Implement standard-library Python with validated indices, iterative path compression, union by size, a same-component query and an explicit component counter.

Write an invariant checker that verifies parent indices, acyclicity, root sizes and component count independently. Explain which checks would detect a faulty merge.

Cross-check against a simple set-partition oracle on deterministic random sequences for small universes. Discuss amortized inverse-Ackermann bounds and why one find operation need not have constant worst-case cost.
Finish with an English/Chinese worked example, a partition certificate after each operation and limitations for deletions, rollback and concurrent updates.

Write standard-library Python functions for reactions and piecewise fields, with tests for midpoint loading, support loading limits and invalid geometry. Include fenced code and a numerical equilibrium check.

Explain why this static calculation alone cannot establish structural safety, deflection or material capacity. Finish with an English/Chinese audit summary distinguishing mathematical checks from engineering design requirements.

Implement standard-library Python using fractions.Fraction and exact Gaussian elimination to solve the transient linear systems. Validate inputs and handle already-absorbed starting states.

turns: Derive the one-panel Simpson quadrature rule on an interval and verify exactness for polynomials of degree at most three. Use LaTeX and distinguish quadrature error from floating-point error.
